basis: Inherited myopia is an ocular refractive and growth disorder.
Dermoids occupy the corneal limbus, cornea and conjunctiva; skin-like histology does not establish skin involvement.
The disease itself is glucocorticoid-induced bone loss and impaired bone strength.
XPA commonly causes neurodegeneration (>50%); chronic ocular surface damage and sensorineural hearing loss each affect roughly >=30% over its course.
Immune-mediated posterior uveitis directly damages the choroid and retina; retinal vessels remain part of the ocular disease.
Corneal dystrophy, keratoderma and skeletal anomalies define the syndrome; enamel abnormalities and caries occur in 80-99%. Hearing impairment is only 5-29%.
Developmental/intellectual disability, congenital heart defects and skeletal/limb anomalies are defining typical features; other organ findings lack common frequencies.
Fibromuscular or muscular obstruction of the left ventricular outflow tract is a cardiac lesion.
Tumor arises in bone or soft connective tissue; sustained tumor-mediated phosphate wasting and hypophosphatemia occur in most. Phosphaturia alone is not renal damage.
Defined by neurodevelopmental and expressive language impairment; variable cardiac anomalies have no evidence of reaching 30%.
The supplied ancestry identifies hereditary phagocyte dysfunction; common organ infiltration or blood-count abnormalities are not established.
Reflex epilepsy is a brain disorder; eating and gastrointestinal sensations trigger seizures without establishing gastrointestinal damage.
IgG4-related inflammatory infiltration and fibrosis form a hepatic pseudotumor; local phlebitis does not establish a separate systemic vascular axis.
Benign epithelial tumor arising from cutaneous sweat glands.
Skeletal muscular dystrophy defines disease; cardiovascular abnormalities are frequent (30-79%). Reduced vital capacity reflects respiratory muscle weakness, not intrinsic lung damage.
Inhaled dust directly produces pulmonary interstitial deposition and injury; autoimmune associations apply only to particular subtypes.
Skeletal dysplasia with craniosynostosis and limb fusions is defining; occipital encephalocele is a defining CNS malformation.
Malignancy originates in intrahepatic bile ducts; sarcomatous differentiation does not change its organ of origin.
GPI biosynthesis disorder with defining CNS disease; osteopenia occurs in 8/8 and myopia in 30-79%. Optic atrophy alone is below threshold (1/10).
Chondrosarcoma is a malignancy of cartilage or related musculoskeletal connective tissue; childhood onset adds no organ axis.
Sphingolipid storage disorder directly demyelinates central and peripheral nerves; weakness, dysphagia and incontinence reflect neurologic dysfunction.
Fallopian tube malignancy is reproductive; no other qualifying organ involvement is established for the umbrella concept.
Defining CNS disease and ectodermal hair abnormalities; skeletal deformities occur in 2/2 assessed, contractures in 1/2; strabismus and ptosis in 2/2. Dysphagia is neurologic.
Hyperplasia is confined to the uterine endometrium, a reproductive tissue outside the axes.
Familial isolated dilated cardiomyopathy directly affects heart muscle; documented in 16/16 patients.
